article.title: The Local: Nov. 12, 2026 news roundup
article.author: The NYC Local - NYC DSA Labor Working Group
article.content: Welcome back to The Local, a publication of NYC-DSA Labor Working Group reporting every two weeks. Send any tips, corrections, and other feedback to thenyclocal@substack.com. In this issue, Mayor Mamdani might be trying to get a progressive union leader to run in 2028, a Cornell study finds that private equity was able to enter and consolidate the home health care industry in New York state due to weak regulation, which also dialectically left it susceptible to one big unionization push by 1199SEIU, and the NYC Ferry unionization drive with TWU propels forward (please drop us a tip with more ferry puns in case this continues, as we are starting to run out). Photo credit: Alexandra Chan at Marcela’s canvass 10/24. Organizing Workers at shelter and supportive housing nonprofit Lantern Community Services are organizing with AFSCME DC37 and demanding voluntary recognition. Editorial employees at Scientific American voted 20-1 to join the Writers Guild of America East. Production assistants at CBS Studios working on the show “Elsbeth” voted 27-0 to join LIUNA Local 724. A unit of postdoc associates and senior postdoc associates at the technically private Research Foundation for the State University of New York located at Stony Brook University voted 92-1 to join the Communications Workers of America. Workers at Adapt Community Network are organizing with the UFT Local 2. The unit of workers at JFK contractors Unifi Aviation we reported on in the last issue filed another representation petition to organize with the TWU. The unionization drive at NYC Ferry continues as a unit of deckhands and senior deckhands organizes with the TWU. Two units of workers at City Squash in the Bronx are organizing as the City Squash Staff Union. Workers at the NYU Langone Sunset Terrace FHC are organizing with 1199SEIU. Workers at LaGuardia Airport contractor Oxford Airport Technical Services are organizing with the International Union of Operating Engineers Local 30. Bargaining & Action The New York Live Arts Workers Union voted to authorize a strike . The Association of Legislative Employees held a lunchtime picket for Legislative division bargaining. Brooklyn nurse and union leader Sarah Dowd, who was suspended without pay by H+H management for holding organizing meetings with nurses on her day off, has been reinstated with full back pay . City Hall A Public Employment Relations Board judge sided with the UFT and found that the city’s Department of Education illegally hired three non-union paraprofessionals at a Bronx elementary school in 2023. [The Chief Leader] Albany The MTA unilaterally cancelled a benefit under which workers who had used more than 50 percent of their sick days could cash them out at retirement in a lump sum payment, leaving the benefit only for workers who had used less than half of their sick days. Workers argued that the unilateral move will, if anything, worsen absenteeism because, past a certain point, it no longer becomes worth it for workers to save their sick days. [The Chief Leader] Two studies released this year by the Cornell University School of Industrial and Labor Relations found that the state’s weak regulatory landscape for home health care allowed private equity to infiltrate the sector, especially when the private equity-backed Public Partnerships LLC was given the contract to administer over half the state’s home health care services. But ironically, the same consolidation has made it possible for 1199SEIU to unionize the 200,000-member workforce in one swoop. [The Chief Leader] Miscellaneous Mayor Mamdani has been meeting with progressive union leaders like Jimmy Williams Jr. (IUPAT), Sara Nelson (AFA-CWA), and Shawn Fain (UAW) to potentially recruit a presidential candidate for 2028. [Axios] The Democratic wave of election victories last Tuesday may, in the near term, pave the way for state and local legislative reforms that benefit workers.
